features.name: fill_alignment_tilt
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Tilt of the candidate bin: how much room is left relative to a perfect fill of it by equal-sized items."""
    r = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float) / capacity
    # w = item/capacity, the fraction the arriving item consumes
    w = float(item) / capacity
    # number of items of exactly this size that would fill the bin, then the leftover fraction
    n_fill = np.floor(r / max(w, 1e-9))
    leftover = r - n_fill * w
    # signed: how well the leftover matches a full item (0 = perfect, near w = worst)
    frac = leftover / max(w, 1e-9)
    # distance from a perfect-fit boundary, in [0,1], 1 = maximal waste
    dist = np.abs(frac - 0.5) * 2.0
    # residual room after placing the item, judged only by whether it lands near empty
    after = np.clip(r - w, 0.0, 1.0)
    # combine: prefer bins where the post-place room is either full-item-aligned or near zero
    score = 1.0 - dist
    return np.clip(score * (1.0 - after) + (1.0 - score) * after, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Tilt of the candidate bin: how much room is left relative to a perfect fill of it by equal-sized items.

features.name: tanh_residual_room_ratio
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Remaining room of each candidate relative to item size, as a signed ratio in [-1,1]."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    c = float(capacity)
    # how much room is left after placing the item, normalised by capacity
    leftover = (bins - item) / c
    # squash to (-1, 1) so huge empty bins don't dominate
    return np.tanh(leftover)
features.measures: Remaining room of each candidate relative to item size, as a signed ratio in [-1,1].

features.name: residual_slack_vs_item_share
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Squared leftover slack after placing the item, relative to capacity, minus the item's own share of that bin."""
    room = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    it = float(item)
    after = np.clip(room - it, 0.0, cap) / cap          # normalised leftover if placed here
    fill_increase = it / np.maximum(room + it, cap)     # how much of the bin's future load the item occupies
    return after * (0.5 - fill_increase)
features.measures: Squared leftover slack after placing the item, relative to capacity, minus the item's own share of that bin.

features.name: best_fit_residual
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Negative post-placement residual scaled by fill: -(bins - item)/capacity * (item/bins), tightest-and-fullest fit highest."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    residual = (bins - item) / cap
    # fraction of the bin that the item fills after placement; smooth, in (0, 1]
    fill = item / np.maximum(bins, 1e-9)
    return -residual * fill

features.name: gated_residual_tightness
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, gated so it only fires when the item nearly fills or overfills the bin; otherwise a mild preference for the fullest bin still fit."""
    # normalized item size
    s = item / capacity
    after = np.clip((bins - item) / capacity, -1.0, 1.0)
    # gate: strong signal when placement leaves very little room (tight fit) or overflows slack
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(0.05 - np.abs(after)) * 40.0))  # ~1 when |after| small
    # near-full preference: bins whose remaining room is close to the item size get boosted
    near = np.exp(-((bins - item) / capacity) ** 2 / 0.02)
    # combine: tight fits pushed down (good for first-fit-decreasing-like behavior), empty bin mildly penalized
    val = -after * (0.5 + 0.5 * tight) + 0.15 * near * (1.0 - tight) - 0.1 * s * tight
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction, gated so it only fires when the item nearly fills or overfills the bin; otherwise a mild preference for the fullest bin still fit.

features.name: graded_near_full_completion
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Graded completion bonus: how close placing the item brings the bin to full, sharpened around near-full fills (smooth, item-relative)."""
    fill_after = (capacity - bins + item) / capacity
    # smooth saturation: near 1 when bin ends almost full, near 0 otherwise
    sharp = np.clip((fill_after - 0.85) / 0.15, -1.0, 1.0)
    bonus = np.sign(sharp) * np.abs(sharp) ** 0.5
    # also credit leaving very little residual relative to the item just placed
    residual = (bins - item) / capacity
    rel = np.clip((0.05 - residual) / 0.05, -1.0, 1.0)
    return np.clip(0.6 * bonus + 0.4 * rel, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Graded completion bonus: how close placing the item brings the bin to full, sharpened around near-full fills (smooth, item-relative).

features.name: tight_fit_gated_residual
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, gated by how tight the fit is relative to the item (sharp best-fit signal)."""
    after = (bins - item) / capacity
    # tightness: how small the leftover is compared to the item size (0 = exact fit, 1 = lots of slack)
    slack_ratio = np.clip((bins - item) / max(item, 1), -1.0, 1.0)
    # sharp gate: exact fits get strongly boosted, loose fits suppressed
    gated = np.tanh(3.0 * (1.0 - np.abs(slack_ratio)))
    return np.clip(after * gated, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction, gated by how tight the fit is relative to the item (sharp best-fit signal).

features.name: residual_modulo
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Preferred when the leftover after placement is an exact multiple of the item size."""
    res = bins - item
    denom = max(item, 1)
    m = np.mod(res, denom)
    return np.clip(1.0 - 2.0 * m / denom, -1.0, 1.0)

idea.hypothesis: Whether a leftover can be *exactly* consumed by further items of the arriving item's size is invisible to residual magnitude. Residual modulo item size is a different arithmetic quantity: small modulo means the leftover is a whole number of such items, so the bin stays reusable rather than becoming scrap.
idea.feature: res = bins - item; m = np.mod(res, max(item, 1)); return np.clip(1.0 - 2.0 * m / max(item, 1), -1.0, 1.0). (Preferred when the leftover is an exact multiple of the item size.)

features.coder_note: This computes, per candidate bin, `1 - 2*(residual mod item)/item` clipped to [-1, 1], so a leftover that is an exact multiple of the item size scores 1 and a leftover just short of a multiple scores near -1; I used `max(item, 1)` as the divisor exactly as specified to guard the modulo.
features.measures: Preferred when the leftover after placement is an exact multiple of the item size.

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, but measured relative to the smaller of the bin's room and the item, so a perfect fit collapses to 0 regardless of scale."""
    after = (bins - item) / capacity
    denom = np.maximum(np.minimum(bins, item), 1.0) / capacity
    ratio = after / np.maximum(denom, 1e-3)
    return np.clip(np.tanh(ratio), -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction, but measured relative to the smaller of the bin's room and the item, so a perfect fit collapses to 0 regardless of scale.

features.name: soft_best_fit_band_with_new_bin_penalty
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction gated by a soft best-fit band relative to item size, with a separate bonus for near-exact fills and a penalty for opening a new bin when a tight fit exists."""
    s = item / capacity
    after = np.clip((bins - item) / capacity, -1.0, 1.0)
    # slack relative to item: how much room would be left, in units of the item size
    slack_ratio = np.clip((bins - item) / max(item, 1), -1.0, 1.5)
    # soft band: strongest when the leftover is a small fraction of the item (near-exact fit)
    band = np.exp(-(slack_ratio ** 2) / 0.35)
    # near-exact fill bonus: leftover under ~5% of capacity gets an extra kick
    exact = np.exp(-(after ** 2) / (2.0 * (0.05 ** 2)))
    # empty-bin discriminator: last candidate is the fresh bin
    is_new = np.zeros_like(after)
    is_new[-1] = 1.0
    # reward tight placements, discourage opening a new bin unless item is large
    val = band * (1.0 - 0.3 * np.abs(after)) + 0.5 * exact - 0.4 * is_new * (1.0 - s)
    # small tie-breaking lean toward the fullest still-fitting bin
    val = val - 0.15 * after
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction gated by a soft best-fit band relative to item size, with a separate bonus for near-exact fills and a penalty for opening a new bin when a tight fit exists.

features.name: item_rhythm_fit
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Signed measure of how close the bin's remaining room is to an integer multiple of the item size (packing-rhythm fit)."""
    b = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    s = max(float(item), 1.0)
    # how many items of this size could still fit
    n = np.floor(b / s)
    leftover = b - n * s  # room that would remain after filling with this item size
    # normalise leftover by the item size: 0 = perfect multiple, near s = worst fit rhythm
    rhythm = leftover / s
    # map to [-1,1]: perfect multiple -> -1 (attractive), worst -> +1
    val = 2.0 * np.clip(rhythm, 0.0, 1.0) - 1.0
    # empty bin: neutral-to-slightly-penalized so it is not blindly preferred
    empty = (b >= capacity - 1e-9)
    val = np.where(empty, 0.0, val)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Signed measure of how close the bin's remaining room is to an integer multiple of the item size (packing-rhythm fit).

features.name: residual_share_of_load
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual normalized by the bin's pre-placement load (fill), so a near-full bin with tiny leftover beats a half-full one with the same leftover."""
    load = capacity - bins  # room used before placement
    after = bins - item     # room left after placement
    # residual share of what was already there; empty bin (load=0) gets a fixed neutral value
    ratio = np.where(load > 0, after / np.maximum(load, 1), after / capacity)
    # emphasise tight fits: split sign by whether the bin ends nearly full vs. still loose
    tight = np.exp(-((after / capacity) ** 2) / 0.01)
    val = np.tanh(2.0 * ratio) * (1.0 - 0.5 * tight)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual normalized by the bin's pre-placement load (fill), so a near-full bin with tiny leftover beats a half-full one with the same leftover.

features.name: complete_midfull_bins
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Negative post-placement residual fraction, gated to bins 50-80% full that fit the item."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    after = (bins - item) / cap
    fill_before = 1.0 - bins / cap
    gate = ((fill_before >= 0.5) & (fill_before <= 0.80) & (bins >= item)).astype(float)
    return np.clip(gate * (-after), -1.0, 1.0)

The 33 under-filled large bins are 50-80% full (residual 0.2-0.5) holding one item; if a 30-50 item arrives they can be completed. Gate tightness on current fill, not |after|, to cash those in.
idea.feature: after=(bins-item)/capacity; fill_before=1-bins/capacity; gate=1.0 where (fill_before>=0.5 and fill_before<=0.80 and bins>=item) else 0; return clip(gate*(-after),-1,1).
idea.lesson: f012 kept on |after| gating but flat in large; re-gate on fill_before to target the 50-80 band

features.coder_note: This computes `-after` (the negated post-placement residual fraction) only for candidate bins whose current fill is between 50% and 80% and that still fit the item, zero elsewhere, clipped to [-1, 1]; I read "bins>=item" as the fit condition and applied the gate to the current fill as specified.

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Size-gated post-placement residual: for large items (s near/above 0.45) reward leaving >=0.45 room or completing, else best-fit."""

    after = (bins - item) / capacity

features.name: fill_cross_half
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """1.0 if placing the item moves the bin's fill from below half to at least half, else 0.0."""
    cap = float(capacity) if capacity else 1.0
    after = (bins - item) / cap
    before_fill = 1.0 - bins / cap
    after_fill = 1.0 - after
    crossed = (before_fill < 0.5) & (after_fill >= 0.5)
    return crossed.astype(float)

idea.hypothesis: f008 (98% threshold) and f011 (graded near-full) were redundant/flat. A crossing test (bin goes from <half full to >=half full) is non-monotone and asks whether crossing the halfway mark attracts items usefully.
idea.feature: after=(bins-item)/capacity; before_fill=1-bins/capacity; after_fill=1-after; return 1.0 where (before_fill<0.5 and after_fill>=0.5) else 0.0.

features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Best-fit residual gated by a two-sided asymmetry: near-exact fits favoured, slight overflow slack penalised more than equal undershoot."""
    item = float(item)
    cap = float(capacity)
    b = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    residual = (b - item) / cap
    # signed relative slack: negative = item doesn't fit well (overshoot), positive = leftover
    rel = (b - item) / max(item, 1.0)
    rel = np.clip(rel, -2.0, 2.0)
    # asymmetric gate: sharp peak at exact fit, decaying faster on the slack side than the tight side
    tight_side = np.exp(-((rel) ** 2) / 0.05)       # narrow peak near rel=0
    slack_side = np.exp(-((rel - 0.6) ** 2) / 0.3)  # broad hump for moderate slack (encourages filling)
    gate = 0.7 * tight_side + 0.3 * slack_side
    # reward positive residual (room left) only when tight; penalise large slack
    val = -np.abs(residual) * gate + 0.15 * residual * (1.0 - gate)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Best-fit residual gated by a two-sided asymmetry: near-exact fits favoured, slight overflow slack penalised more than equal undershoot.

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, measured relative to the candidate's own remaining room (relative fill error), clipped."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    it = float(item)
    after = bins - it

    denom = np.maximum(bins, 1.0)
    rel = after / denom

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement leftover measured against the item size, signed by whether the bin ends nearly empty or nearly full (asymmetric V-shape)."""

def feature(item, bins, capacity):

features.name: adaptive_gate_fillweighted_residual
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Tight-fit gate relative to item, but measured against the *pre-placement* fullness so that a nearly-full bin fitted exactly is ranked below a half-full bin fitted exactly, and the gate width scales with item size."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    it = float(max(item, 1))
    after = (bins - it) / cap
    # slack relative to item, signed: 0 = exact fit, 1 = empty bin fits item with lots of room
    slack_ratio = np.clip((bins - it) / it, -1.0, 1.0)
    # gate width adapts: big items -> narrow gate (only near-exact fits count), small items -> wider
    width = 1.5 + 3.0 * (it / cap)
    gated = np.tanh(width * (1.0 - np.abs(slack_ratio)))
    # fullness before placement: prefer exact fits into bins that also end up well filled
    fill_before = np.clip(1.0 - bins / cap, 0.0, 1.0)
    # combine: residual (gated) tilted by pre-fill so exact fits into fuller bins win
    val = after * gated * (0.5 + 0.5 * fill_before)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Tight-fit gate relative to item, but measured against the *pre-placement* fullness so that a nearly-full bin fitted exactly is ranked below a half-full bin fitted exactly, and the gate width scales with item size.

features.name: relative_residual_vs_preroom
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, but measured relative to the bin's current fill level instead of raw capacity (relative waste)."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    s = item / cap
    after = bins - item                       # remaining room after placement
    # normalize the residual by the room the bin HAD before placement, not by capacity:
    # a big absolute residual in a nearly-empty bin is cheap, the same residual in a
    # nearly-full bin is expensive. Guard against tiny/zero pre-room.
    before = np.clip(bins / cap, 1e-3, 1.0)
    rel = after / (bins + 1e-6)               # leftover as a fraction of pre-placement room
    rel = np.clip(rel, -1.0, 1.0)
    # blend with raw residual so tight fits in full bins and roomy fits in empty bins are separated
    val = 0.5 * rel + 0.5 * np.clip(after / cap, -1.0, 1.0)
    # empty bin gets a small fixed nudge: it "wastes" a whole fresh bin
    empty = (before >= 0.999).astype(float)
    val = val - 0.05 * empty * s
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction, but measured relative to the bin's current fill level instead of raw capacity (relative waste).

features.name: residual_item_alignment
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Rank candidates by how close the post-placement residual is to a whole multiple of the item size (alignment of remaining room with the item)."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    resid = bins - item
    s = float(item) / cap
    # normalized residual in [-1, 1]
    r = np.clip(resid / cap, -1.0, 1.0)
    # residual measured in units of item size (guard small items)
    units = resid / max(float(item), 1.0)
    # distance to nearest whole number of item-sized pieces (0 = perfectly aligned)
    frac = np.abs(units - np.round(units))
    # alignment score: 1 when residual is a whole multiple of item, decreasing with mismatch
    align = 1.0 - 2.0 * np.clip(frac, 0.0, 1.0)
    # only meaningful when the item actually fits and some room remains
    fits = (bins >= item).astype(float)
    val = fits * align * (0.4 + 0.6 * (1.0 - np.abs(r))) * (0.5 + 0.5 * s)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Rank candidates by how close the post-placement residual is to a whole multiple of the item size (alignment of remaining room with the item).

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Sign of post-placement slack times a fit-quality gate: rewards the bin whose leftover best matches the item's own size scale."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    s = item / cap
    after = (bins - item) / cap
    # leftover relative to the item size, signed: -1 overfull, 0 exact, +1 lots of slack
    ratio = (bins - item) / max(item, 1)
    ratio = np.clip(ratio, -1.0, 1.0)
    # gate peaks when the leftover is comparable to the item size (ratio near 0.5),
    # not at exact fit: reflects that leaving room for a same-sized partner is good
    gate = np.exp(-((ratio - 0.5) ** 2) / 0.08)
    # sign term: prefer underfull-ish leftovers over overfull, but let the gate dominate
    sign = np.tanh(4.0 * ratio)
    val = gate * sign * (0.7 + 0.6 * s)
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Sign of post-placement slack times a fit-quality gate: rewards the bin whose leftover best matches the item's own size scale.

features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Post-placement residual fraction, but only trusted when it stays in a middle band; otherwise replaced by a fill-ratio ramp, so differently-slack bins separate."""
    after = (bins - item) / capacity
    fill_before = 1.0 - bins / capacity          # how full the bin already is (0 empty, 1 full)
    # band gate: peak signal for residuals in [0.15, 0.5], fade outside
    band = np.exp(-((np.abs(after) - 0.32) ** 2) / (2 * 0.18 ** 2))
    # complement branch: a monotone ramp on pre-existing fullness, active where the band is silent
    ramp = 2.0 * fill_before - 1.0               # in [-1, 1]
    val = band * (0.5 - after) + (1.0 - band) * ramp
    return np.clip(val, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Post-placement residual fraction, but only trusted when it stays in a middle band; otherwise replaced by a fill-ratio ramp, so differently-slack bins separate.

def feature(item, bins, capacity):

nodes.description: Tilt of the candidate bin: how much room is left relative to a perfect fill of it by equal-sized items.

nodes.title: size_gated_best_fit
nodes.description: Apply tightest-fit preference only when the item is large relative to capacity, and spread otherwise, so large items don't strand half-empty bins.

nodes.title: future_large_capacity
nodes.description: Score a bin by whether its post-placement residual can still accept a typical large item (e.g. ~0.5 capacity), rewarding residuals near 0 or above that threshold.

nodes.title: residual_modulo_fit
nodes.description: Measure residual room modulo item size to reward leftovers that equal-sized items can exactly consume.

nodes.title: residual_band_avoidance
nodes.description: Penalise post-placement residuals that fall in the wasteful 0.5-0.8 capacity band where neither another large nor several small items fit well.

nodes.title: item_size_conditional_tightness
nodes.description: Switch between tightest-fit and spread based on the arriving item's size relative to capacity, so small items pack tightly and large items keep room.

nodes.title: wide find: item_rhythm_fit
nodes.description: Signed measure of how close the bin's remaining room is to an integer multiple of the item size (packing-rhythm fit).

nodes.title: large_pairing_residual
nodes.description: For large items, prefer the bin whose post-placement residual is either near-zero (completes) or large enough (>=0.45 cap) to pair with another large item, avoiding the 0.1-0.4 dead zone.

nodes.title: single_item_bin_avoidance
nodes.description: Penalise opening a new bin or leaving a bin with only the arriving item when an existing bin could absorb it, targeting the 38 single-item bins in the large family.

nodes.title: age_tiebreak
nodes.description: Break near-ties in fit by bin age: among candidates whose post-placement residual is within a small margin, prefer the oldest bin so long-lived bins get filled instead of lingering.

nodes.title: pool_residual_diversity
nodes.description: Score each candidate by whether its residual is duplicated elsewhere in the pool (safe to consume) and its leftover is novel (a new capability), keeping the pool's set of usable residuals rich.

nodes.title: wide find: residual_item_alignment
nodes.description: Rank candidates by how close the post-placement residual is to a whole multiple of the item size (alignment of remaining room with the item).
